title: Promoting Real-Time Reflection in Synchronous Communication with Generative AI
venue: ACM Workshop on Human-AI Interaction for Augmented Reasoning (AIREASONING-2025-01)
extended_summary:
This position paper examines how real-time reflection can be supported in synchronous communication using generative AI. The authors argue that reflection is valuable during live interactions because it helps speakers adjust their communication strategies in the moment, but existing systems often focus on post-hoc reflection rather than during-activity support.

Rather than reporting a new empirical study, the paper reviews 11 recent systems across synchronous communication scenarios such as online meetings, lectures, presentations, and practice talks. These systems include tools for aggregating audience status, visualizing conversation summaries, simulating audience feedback, and providing expert suggestions. The authors compare how these systems support reflection, the interaction paradigms they use, and the degree to which they rely on generative AI versus traditional NLP/CV techniques.

The paper concludes that generative AI opens new opportunities for richer, more contextual real-time reflection by generating nuanced summaries, role-playing as audiences or experts, and producing timely suggestions. It also identifies design challenges, especially interpretability, timing of proactive feedback, and the limitations of role-play agents in specialized contexts. The paper’s main contribution is a set of design implications for building human-AI interaction systems that scaffold real-time reflection without disrupting synchronous work.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper and design-oriented review, not an empirical evaluation of an intervention or outcome. It synthesizes prior work and proposes design implications without a clear study design, causal comparison, or measured educational effects.
impact_tier_rationale: No K-12 achievement, reasoning, vocabulary, retention, or engagement impact is reported. The paper is speculative/conceptual for synchronous communication support, so there is no measurable impact evidence to score.

interventions.use_case: conceptual review of generative AI/LLM use for real-time reflection support in synchronous communication, including simulating audience feedback, providing expert suggestions, and generating real-time summaries or dialogue mappings
AI systems that provide immediate personalized feedback or actionable suggestions during live communication, such as TutorUp-style expert feedback for novice tutors
learning-status and audience-status analytics that aggregate cues in real time to help instructors or speakers monitor learner engagement and communication effectiveness
